shortDescription: Egypt's non-oil private sector contracted at its softest pace since January in August as declines in output and new orders eased and firms stepped up hiring, a business survey showed on Thursday.

children: Egypt's non-oil private sector contracted at its softest pace since January in August as declines in output and new orders eased and firms stepped up hiring, a business survey showed on Thursday.
The seasonally adjusted S&P Global Egypt Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) rose to 49.6 in August from 46.8 in July, its highest reading in seven months.
The 50 mark separates growth from contraction.

"The Egypt PMI demonstrated increased signs of economic recovery across the non-oil sector in August, with the headline index rising nearly three points on the month," said David Owen, principal economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence.

Output fell at the slowest pace in seven months, while new business remained in contraction but declined at the weakest rate since February. Export sales also fell, extending a six-month downturn, though the pace eased from July.

Employment rose for the first time since last October and at the second-fastest rate since the survey began in 2011. Backlogs of work broadly stabilised after rising in each of the previous three months.

Purchasing activity shrank for a fifth straight month and at the fastest pace in nearly three years, as firms cited material shortages and cash-flow constraints. Supplier delivery times also deteriorated modestly after July's brief improvement.

Price pressures accelerated for the first time since May, with both input costs and output charges rising faster. Business sentiment improved for a fourth time in five months to its highest since June 2022, with firms linking optimism to new projects, tourism and branch openings.
